No, because this is likely a strict liability law that does not provide for defenses based on mental state.

Yes, because the law does not explicitly state that the driver of the vehicle is responsible for the actions of the passengers.

\[ \text{Markup based on cost} = 0.25 \times C \]

\[ \text{Percent markup based on cost} = 0.25 \times 100 \]

question: Four years ago the owner of a shopping center leased a store in the center for a 10-year term to a pharmacistfor use as a drugstore. Last year the owner purchased a parcel of land immediately adjacent to the shopping center. That parcel wasimproved with a building that, at the time of the owner's purchase and for ten years earlier, was occupied inpart by a food supermarket and in part by a discount drugstore, under leases which the prior owner assignedto the owner. The owner reconstructed the common facilities of both shopping centers to integrate them and combine themso that, to the public, the two centers appeared as a larger single development. question: A homeowner buys a new leaf blower and is so impressed with its power that he gets carried away and blows large amounts of his work onto the next door neighbor's yard. In addition to leaves, he also blew large amounts of pest-infested plant debris onto the neighbor's property. The material has accumulated into large, unsightly piles and caused damage to the neighbor's healthy plants. He has to pay workers to haul the material away and he incurs expenses to replace infected perennials. The neighbor sues for the tort of trespass. The homeowner files a motion to dismiss because the neighbor cannot prove that homeowner acted with an intent to trespass or to do harm. Will the court grant the motion to dismiss?
options: Yes, because the homeowner expected the wind to carry the debris away and did not think that it would accumulate on the neighbor's property.
No, because the homeowner's actions resulted in a direct invasion of the neighbor's property.
Yes, because the debris was not intentionally directed at the neighbor's property.
Yes, because the homeowner was not aware of the pest-infested debris.
No, because the neighbor was able to prove financial loss from the damage caused.
No, because trespass is based on an intentional act of entering the land or sending something onto the land, and the actor does not have to intend harm to be liable for the tort.
Yes, because the homeowner had no practical way of controlling where the material went and he acted without malice or ill will.
Yes, because the homeowner did not physically enter the neighbor's property.
No, because the infected debris constituted an abnormally dangerous condition and homeowner could be held strictly liable for the trespass.
No, because the act of blowing debris onto the neighbor's land constitutes a trespass regardless of intent.
gold: No, because trespass is based on an intentional act of entering the land or sending something onto the land, and the actor does not have to intend harm to be liable for the tort.

H) The man will not acquire title unless he continues in adverse possession for an additional 12years, or nine years after the son attains the ageof 18.
I) The man will acquire title by adverse possession only if he continues in possession for a total of 30 years.
